title: Population Ecology
seo_title: Grade 11 Life Sciences: Population Ecology Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: Population size and density; estimating population size by quadrats and mark–recapture; population growth curves (geometric and logistic); carrying capacity and limiting factors; interactions in communities: competition, predation and symbiosis; social organisation; ecological succession. (summary of CAPS Life Sciences, Grade 11, Life Sciences: Population ecology)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Life Sciences worksheets (CAPS): population size, quadrats, mark–recapture, growth curves, carrying capacity, competition, predation and symbiosis. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Carrying capacity is the largest population an environment can support.
body_html:
How to think about it

Population size can be estimated with quadrats (for plants and slow animals) or the mark–recapture method: N = (number first marked × number caught second time) ÷ number recaptured with marks.

With unlimited resources a population grows geometrically (J-shaped curve); in nature, limiting factors such as food, space and disease slow growth, giving a logistic (S-shaped) curve that levels off at the carrying capacity. Organisms interact by competition, predation and symbiosis (mutualism, commensalism, parasitism).

Example

40 marked; later 50 caught, 10 marked. Estimate N.

(40 × 50)/10

Answer: 200

Example

Oxpeckers eat ticks off buffalo. Which interaction?

Both benefit.

Answer: mutualism

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying the wrong numbers in mark–recapture.
  • Thinking a population can grow forever.
  • Mixing up commensalism and mutualism.

faq.q: Why do predator and prey numbers rise and fall in cycles?
faq.a: More prey means more food for predators; then predators eat more prey, prey fall, and predators fall after them.

items.q: Scientists mark 77 turtles and release them. Later they catch 47, and 11 are marked. Estimate the population (N = marked × caught ÷ recaptured).
A pond has 420 lotus plants. Last year 78 new plants were added by reproduction. What is the birth rate per plant per year?
items.e: Birth rate = new individuals ÷ population = 78 ÷ 420 = 0,186.
